summary: Tested the Pitch Summary PDF feature on both backend and frontend, using 2 fresh +clerk_test users (A owns a demo workspace, B owns a separate demo workspace). Exactly 2 Testnet transactions: a 25 XLM API seed payment and a 5 XLM payment from the full UI tour. Backend: 15 of 15 pytest cases pass. (1) An unconfirmed payment returns 409. (2) A confirmed payment returns application/pdf with attachment filename agos-pitch-summary.pdf, exactly 1 page. (3) duration 0, 7201, -5 and 'abc' each return 422; durations 1 and 7200 render 'in 0:01' and 'in 120:00'. (4) The PDF contains the title 'From expense to verified settlement in 1:44', synthetic KPI boxes, the timeline, the full tx hash, ledger, source, destination, the Horizon verification line, the explorer URL (also a clickable link) and the disclaimers. (5) Isolation: user B's token with B's workspace gets 404, B's token with A's workspace id gets 404, no auth gets 401, an unknown id gets 404, and an expense_id from another workspace is silently ignored. (6) Role scope: an employee persona (X-Act-As Paolo) gets 404 on the owner's payment and 200 on his own payment. Rendering with pymupdf: no overlapping text with normal data, but text overlaps when the merchant name is long (see issues). Frontend: the full 6-step tour completed, and tour-download-pdf-btn downloaded agos-pitch-summary.pdf. That PDF is 1 page, titled 'in 0:13', has the full timeline including 'Expense submitted: Figma (investor tour)' and 'Expense approved', ledger 5882184, and no overlap. In the Payments drawer, pitch-pdf-btn is shown for the confirmed payment and downloads the PDF; it is not shown for the pending_approval payment. No console errors.

minor.issue: The step description is cut at 80 characters, not at a measured width. Because of that, long text runs into the right-aligned timestamp. Reproduced with an expense merchant of 74 characters (merchant allows up to 120): 'TEST_Very Long Merchant Name Professional Services Corporation International · PHP ...' overlaps '23 Nov 2026, 11:48 UTC' by 43pt (seen in the pymupdf render). recipient_name (up to 120 characters) can cause the same problem on the 'Payment requested' line. Fix: fit the text to the available width (W - M - timestamp width - (M+140) - gap) using stringWidth or simpleSplit, then add an ellipsis or wrap it.

The subtitle (workspace name, location, generated time) is not width-checked. A long real-workspace name or location would run off the right edge of the page. Not reproduced, because demo workspace names are fixed. Use simpleSplit or truncate it.

When the PDF is downloaded from the Payments drawer (no expense_id), the title still reads 'From expense to verified settlement', but the timeline has no expense steps. Consider a title such as 'Verified settlement' when no expense is given.
Timestamps show minutes only. In a 13-second tour, all 6 timeline steps show the same '23 Nov 2026, 11:49 UTC', which weakens the 'what happened' story. Consider showing HH:MM:SS.

ui_bugs.issue: The useElapsed timer keeps running after the tour finishes. The headline 'Settled and verified in {elapsed}' went from 0:13 to 0:16 while the panel stayed open, but the downloaded PDF correctly says 0:13 (ctx.duration). Investors see two different durations. Fix: when done, show ctx.duration formatted as M:SS, or stop the timer.

issues: Roughly the bottom 20% of the A4 page is empty. The layout is otherwise clean, has good contrast and the QR code is legible. Optional: move the disclaimers to the bottom of the page as a footer.

action_items: Stop the tour completion timer, or show ctx.duration in 'Settled and verified in …', so it matches the PDF
Fit the timeline description text in pitch_pdf.py to the available width so long merchant or recipient names do not overlap the timestamp
Width-check the header subtitle (workspace name and location)
Optional: change the title when there is no expense_id; show seconds in timeline timestamps
critical_code_review_comments: downloadFile uses responseType 'blob'. On errors, axios gives a Blob body, so errMsg(e) probably cannot read the JSON 'detail' (for example the 409 message) and shows a generic error. Parse the blob text before showing the toast.
pitch_summary runs refresh_stellar, which calls Horizon, on every download and swallows all exceptions. That is acceptable, but a slow Horizon response will delay the PDF. Consider a timeout.

Seeded 'approved' demo expenses have only a pending_approval history entry and no 'approved' entry. A PDF for one of them therefore skips the 'Expense approved' step, and its 'submitted' time is the seeding time, not the expense date. This is a seed data inconsistency.

success_rate.backend: 100% (15/15 pytest); 1 layout overlap found with long input
success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested flows; 1 medium timer mismatch

seed_data_creation: Created agos.t5pdfA+clerk_test and agos.t5pdfB+clerk_test (2 demo workspaces), 1 TEST_Pending contractor payment, 1 TEST_ long-merchant expense, and 2 Testnet txs (25 XLM API, 5 XLM tour). Deleted everything afterwards by workspace id and user id: all workspace-scoped docs, the workspaces, the users docs and the Clerk users. No other data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `python /app/backend/tests/pdf_setup.py`. It is idempotent, does at most 1 Testnet tx, and writes /tmp/pdf_state.json (ticketA, wsA/wsB, confirmed/unconfirmed payment ids). Then run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_pitch_pdf.py` and `python /app/backend/tests/pdf_overlap.py <file.pdf>` (checks span overlap and renders a PNG). To test the overlap fix, create an expense with a merchant of more than 70 characters, approve it, and pass it as expense_id. Sign-in tickets are single-use, so re-run pdf_setup.py for each browser session.
